artifacts.summary: Confirms multi-glob paths: syntax via existing precedent, empirically resolves AC7 (paths: auto-load fires on Read/Edit/Write only, never on Bash), and supplies ready-to-apply text for the rule's new Continuous Build Safety section, the EXTENSION.md pointer, the compilation-guide.md cross-reference, and a one-pointer addition to latex-implementation-agent.md; recommends the three absorbed mechanism tasks stay deferred/not-admitted this round.

memory_candidates.content: The Claude Code harness's rule paths: frontmatter auto-load (agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/context-discovery.md's 'Rule Loading: Two Independent Paths') fires only on Read/Edit/Write tool calls whose path matches the glob. It does NOT fire on a Bash tool call whose command string names, or even cat's the content of, a matching path. Verified empirically in-session with a minimal pair: `cat` on a real .lua file via Bash produced no rule injection, while a Read tool call on the identical file immediately injected the full matching rule. Any always-in-effect guidance meant to cover bare Bash tool invocations must live in an eager CLAUDE.md merge-source pointer (or an equivalent unconditional channel), not rely on widening a rule's paths: glob alone.

Multi-glob paths: frontmatter (JSON-array-of-quoted-strings form, e.g. paths: ["a/**", "b/**"]) is already an established, deployed pattern in this codebase's rule files (core/rules/git-workflow.md, nvim/rules/neovim-lua.md, web/rules/web-astro.md, nix/rules/nix.md), and is explicitly parsed by measure-eager-context.sh's rule_matches_rep_paths logic. No manifest.json change or loader change is needed to add a second/third glob to an existing single-glob rule.
